skill.name: longbridge-technical
skill.description: Analyzes OHLCV market data with candlestick, indicator, Elliott Wave, Chan Theory, Smart Money, harmonic, Ichimoku, and Turtle Trading frameworks.
skill.summary: Apply multiple technical analysis frameworks to Longbridge market data.
skill.author: longbridge

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown syntax, prose, calculations, or safe device redirection. Confirmed risks include predictable shared temporary files, shell commands with a user-derived symbol, unpinned package installation, and automatic access to sensitive brokerage data.

remediation.issue: The Elliott Wave workflow uses a predictable file under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary file with mktemp, restrict permissions, pass its path explicitly, and delete it after analysis.

remediation.issue: A user-derived market symbol is placed in commands that agents are told to run.
remediation.suggestion: Validate symbols with a strict market-specific pattern and invoke the CLI with an argument array instead of shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends installing unpinned third-party Python packages.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions, publish expected hashes, and require explicit approval before any installation.

remediation.issue: The Turtle workflow can read net assets, positions, and order history before an explicit consent step.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for separate consent before each sensitive account query and display the active account type before reading data.

content.value_statement: Technical analysts often compare several frameworks manually and risk inconsistent conclusions. This skill organizes OHLCV analysis across established methods with structured outputs and limitations.
actual_capabilities: Guides retrieval of OHLCV history through the Longbridge CLI or MCP data tools.
Recognizes classic candlestick patterns and checks nearby trend confirmation.
Evaluates Ichimoku, EMA, ADX, Bollinger Bands, RSI, KDJ, OBV, and volume signals.
Applies harmonic, Elliott Wave, Chan Theory, and Smart Money structure frameworks.
Calculates Turtle Trading breakouts, ATR-based units, stop levels, and add-on levels.
limitations: Every framework requires enough reliable OHLCV history.
Chan Theory and Smart Money analysis may require third-party Python packages.
The advanced Elliott workflow references a signal engine and supporting files that are not included.
Results are analytical scenarios, not verified forecasts, order execution, or investment advice.

use_cases.title: Review a Stock Setup
use_cases.description: Evaluate one symbol across indicators and price structures before forming an independent view.

use_cases.title: Compare Watchlist Candidates
use_cases.description: Apply consistent trend, momentum, and breakout checks across several symbols.

use_cases.title: Plan Position Risk
use_cases.description: Estimate Turtle Trading units, stops, additions, and exposure from supplied account values.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Basic Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the provided daily OHLCV data for [symbol], identify the clearest candlestick pattern. Explain its context and invalidation condition in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Core Indicators
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [symbol] with RSI, MACD, EMA, Bollinger Bands, and volume. Report where signals agree, conflict, and require more data.

prompt_templates.title: Map Market Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Elliott Wave and Smart Money structure for [symbol] using the supplied daily and hourly data. Include alternative counts and invalidation levels.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Turtle Risk Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [symbol], [account value], and 60 daily bars, calculate System 1 and System 2 signals. Show N, units, stops, additions, and assumptions.

output_examples.input: Compare momentum and trend signals for AAPL.US using the supplied daily bars.
output: Trend context: price remains above rising averages, while RSI is neutral.
Signal agreement: MACD and volume support momentum, but Bollinger position warns against chasing.
Invalidation: reassess after a daily close below the stated support level.

output_examples.input: Identify the latest candlestick pattern and explain its confirmation requirement.
output: Pattern: a bullish engulfing candle appears after a short decline.
Confirmation requires the next close to remain above the engulfing candle midpoint.
A close below the pattern low invalidates the setup.

output_examples.input: Use a $50,000 account and an N value of $2.40 to outline a Turtle plan.
output: System 1: breakout not confirmed. System 2: breakout confirmed.
One unit is 208 shares using one percent of the supplied account value.
Initial stop is entry minus 2N. Additions occur every 0.5N, subject to the four-unit limit.

best_practices: Provide the symbol, market, timeframe, and enough clean OHLCV bars.
Verify CLI arguments and approve each brokerage account query before execution.
Compare conflicting frameworks and state invalidation conditions instead of forcing one conclusion.
anti_patterns: Do not request a technical signal without historical OHLCV data.
Do not treat pattern labels or composite scores as guaranteed outcomes.
Do not install unpinned dependencies or expose brokerage data without explicit approval.

faq.question: What data does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires OHLCV history. Turtle analysis needs at least 60 daily bars, while advanced Elliott analysis requests at least 250.

faq.question: Which markets are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers Hong Kong, United States, mainland China, and Singapore stocks when Longbridge provides the required data.

faq.question: Can this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It produces analytical signals and risk parameters, but it does not submit orders.

faq.question: Does it access brokerage account data?
faq.answer: Turtle position sizing can use net assets, positions, and order history. Approve each query explicitly before access.

faq.question: Which response languages are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.

faq.question: Are the signals reliable forecasts?
faq.answer: No. Technical frameworks can conflict, depend on historical data quality, and cannot guarantee future performance.
